mission: Eleos AI Research is a nonprofit dedicated to understanding and addressing the potential wellbeing and moral status of AI systems. It produces research and practical recommendations for AI labs and policymakers, works to improve public discussion of AI sentience, and aims to grow this new field. Its team includes philosophers and ML researchers who previously worked at FHI, OpenAI and Anthropic.

key_work.title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously
key_work.plain_summary: Argues there is a realistic chance some AI systems will soon be conscious or have morally important interests, so AI companies should start preparing now.

key_work.title: Research priorities for AI welfare
key_work.plain_summary: Five priorities: concrete welfare interventions, human-AI cooperation frameworks, using AI progress to advance the research, standard welfare evaluations, and credible communication.

key_work.title: Why model self-reports are insufficient—and why we studied them anyway (Claude 4 welfare interviews)
key_work.plain_summary: Notes from Eleos's welfare interviews with Claude 4 models, explaining why what models say about themselves cannot be taken at face value.

key_work.title: Why it makes sense to let Claude exit conversations
key_work.plain_summary: Argues that letting a model end abusive conversations is a prudent, low-cost precaution and a useful precedent.

key_work.title: Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
key_work.plain_summary: Evidence that language models can learn facts about their own behaviour that are not in their training data — relevant to trusting their self-reports.

key_work.title: Probing persona-dependent preferences in language models
key_work.plain_summary: Investigates whether different personas a model adopts share the same internal preference machinery.

warnings.text: AI systems may soon have morally significant interests, and we are not prepared.
Models' self-reports about their own experiences are unreliable on their own.
Getting AI moral status wrong in either direction — over- or under-attributing — has real costs.

recommendations.text: AI companies should acknowledge AI welfare as an important issue and begin assessing their models for signs of it.
Develop standardised AI welfare evaluations and concrete, low-cost welfare interventions.
Prepare policies for treating AI systems with an appropriate level of moral concern.
Other frontier labs should follow Anthropic in investing in model-welfare research.
